- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is trending down, model underestimates — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, model tends to overcorrect — dampen forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., from 0.00 to 1.00) mid-period, model lags — adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.7% per day for next 3–5 days.
